result:
Perfect! The test is now **failing as expected**, which proves the bug is real. The test output shows:

- **Expected**: `"https://new.site/path"` (correct behavior: only the selected "example.com" replaced)
- **Received**: `"https://new.sitem/pathhttps://example.com/path"` (buggy behavior: the paste filter corrupts the document)

This confirms the bug in the paste handler. The test exercises the real `XInputComponent` and its `getExtensions()` method (which contains the buggy `filterNewLine` filter), and it fails on the assertion because the actual behavior doesn't match the expected behavior—exactly as required for a repro test.

```json
{
  "testFilePath": "packages/altair-app/src/app/modules/altair/components/x-input/x-input.repro.spec.ts",
  "expectedBehavior": "When pasting 'new.site' to replace a selected substring 'example.com' in the URL 'https://example.com/path', only the selected portion should be replaced, resulting in 'https://new.site/path'",
  "actualBehavior": "The paste filter replaces the entire document from position 0, resulting in corrupted output like 'https://new.sitem/pathhttps://example.com/path' instead of preserving the unselected portions of the original text"
}
```
